title: GH #84: companion teardown only after the merge's dirty-tree checks pass
action: BUGFIX, red-first: write the repro test and see it fail BEFORE the fix. In packages/bee/lib/worktree-store.mjs mergeFeatureWorktreeStage: teardownCompanionIfPresent (:1699, sole caller repo-wide) runs BEFORE both dirty-tree checks (:1701, :1704), so ANY merge invocation against a --with-companion worktree destroys the mount (symlink + .bee/companion-session.json + best-effort session end) even when the merge is then refused. The old ordering exists because the mounted symlink is untracked and isTreeDirty(worktreeRoot) would refuse every companion merge (doc comment :1585-1612). FIX (plan-checked, empirically verified): (1) read the marker WITHOUT deleting to learn marker.mountPath — mountPath is relative to worktreeRoot, may contain slashes, validated no-leading-/ no-.. (validateCompanionMountPath :651-663; written verbatim :715-717). (2) Worktree dirty check uses a git PATHSPEC EXCLUSION, NOT text filtering of porcelain output: git status --porcelain -- ':(exclude)<mountPath>' (normalize backslashes to forward slashes first). Text filtering is WRONG for nested mounts — porcelain collapses vendor/repo to '?? vendor/', the mountPath line never appears, and the merge would refuse forever (verified against git 2.43.0); quoting ('?? "my repo"') is also live. A dirty file OTHER than the mount still refuses. (3) Move the teardown call to AFTER ALL zero-mutation refusals — not merely after the two dirty checks: WORKTREE_MERGE_DETACHED_HEAD (:1713) and WORKTREE_MERGE_BRANCH_MISMATCH (:1737) would otherwise still destroy the mount. Insert just before the first mutation at :1747 (preMergeHead; 'everything above is zero-mutation' comment :1741-1746). The companion variable stays in scope for every later consumer (:1775, :1793, :1820, :1868, :1922) — nothing between :1699 and :1747 reads it, and nothing later assumes the companion is already gone. ACCEPTED RESIDUAL (state in trace): post-staging outcomes (MERGE_CONFLICT, red verify) still tear down — unavoidable without violating reason 2 (session must not outlive a proceeding merge). Update the stale doc comments (:1585-1612, :1696-1698) to the new ordering. Tests in packages/bee/tests/test_worktree_store.mjs (reuse makeOrdinaryRepoFixture :36, mergeableWorktreeFixture :161; no companion test exists there yet): (a) refused merge preserves mount: marker + real untracked symlink + one genuinely dirty file -> WORKTREE_MERGE_WORKTREE_DIRTY AND marker+symlink still exist; (b) clean companion merge with a NESTED mountPath (e.g. vendor/companion — this is the case text-filtering would break) succeeds AND tears down marker+symlink; (c) no-marker worktree: no-op path unchanged; (d) detached-HEAD or branch-mismatch refusal also preserves the mount. End-to-end coverage: scripts/tests/test_worktree_companion.mjs case 3 (:205-238) runs real --with-companion create+merge against the VENDORED .bee/bin/bee.mjs (:30) — in verify, and only meaningful AFTER the regen. REGEN OBLIGATION (repo law), run BEFORE final verify: node scripts/render_plugin_skill_trees.mjs; node packages/bee/scripts/onboard_bee.mjs --repo-root . --apply; node scripts/release_manifest.mjs --write. Commit regenerated files in the same cell commit.

truths: A merge refused by either dirty-tree check leaves the companion mount (symlink + marker) fully intact.
A clean --with-companion merge still succeeds and still tears the companion down (the untracked symlink never blocks it).
A worktree without a companion marker behaves byte-identically to today.
All existing test_worktree_store checks stay green.
artifacts: failing-then-passing test output captured in the cell trace
prohibitions: Do not delete or weaken teardownCompanionIfPresent's best-effort/never-throw contract.
No product-file edits outside the two listed product files (regen outputs excepted).
